title: RAW UNREVIEWED: mandatory short subcodes and capacity of general uniquely decodable letter tables
summary: A source-free necessary bound for arbitrary finite uniquely decodable letter codes with at most22 entries, without prefix- or suffix-freeness. Whole one-unit groups force singleton codes. For each exact candidate singleton set, whole two-unit groups force a finite subcode; a non-UD subcode excludes every extension, while actual word-start branches impose further code counts without double counting. Identity remains possible; the question concerns an actually used multi-unit code. No native application or full-code solver is supplied.

contract.A: Fixed finite working-unit alphabet, contemplated size22. Every unit in A is assumed to occur somewhere in the bounded input W for the proper-S nontriviality shortcut. If this is not true, use the observed-unit set for that shortcut or state the missing premise explicitly.
contract.W: A finite set of original complete written word-group strings over A. Whole-group boundaries and working-unit atomicity are explicit conditional assumptions. Multi-character unit labels are not split into ASCII characters.
contract.C: An unknown fixed finite set of distinct nonempty strings over A, one injectively assigned code per source character, with |C|<=22. Every w in W must be in C*. Code lengths are arbitrary finite positive integers.
contract.UD: Free unique decodability: two finite sequences of codewords with the same concatenation must be the same codeword sequence. This applies to all code sequences, not merely attested words or grammar-approved source strings.
contract.nontriviality: At least one multi-unit code is actually used in the unique parse of some w in W. A merely unused longer entry is irrelevant.
contract.not_assumed: No prefix-free or suffix-free property, no maximum code length, no source dictionary, grammar, language, native word value, hidden code boundaries, state-dependent variants, deletions or padding.

mandatory_subcode_theorem.W1: Units that occur as original complete one-unit groups.
mandatory_subcode_theorem.W2: The set of original complete two-unit strings ab. These are not arbitrary substrings and are not prefix/right quotients derived under an inapplicable stronger code premise.
mandatory_subcode_theorem.S0: W1, necessarily singleton codes because a nonempty one-unit string cannot be composed from longer nonempty codes.
mandatory_subcode_theorem.S: The exact singleton-code set of a proposed C, viewed as units in A; S0 subset S subset A.
mandatory_subcode_theorem.B_S: B(S) = {singleton a : a in S} union {two-unit string ab in W2 : a not in S or b not in S}.
mandatory_subcode_theorem.proof: A two-unit whole group has only two possible code-boundary patterns: one length2 code ab, or two singleton codes a and b. If either singleton is absent, ab itself is mandatory. If both singletons are present, adding ab as a code would violate UD immediately via [ab] versus [a,b]. Thus B(S) is a mandatory subset of every compatible C with exact singleton set S.
mandatory_subcode_theorem.heredity: If B(S) is non-UD, its two unequal code sequences remain a collision in every superset C, so that S is impossible. If B(S) is UD, extension/coverage is unresolved; UD is not preserved under arbitrary additions.
mandatory_subcode_theorem.capacity: Every compatible C has at least |B(S)| entries. B(S) is a set: repeated observed forms do not count as additional code entries.

additional_original_word_head_bound.d_h: For each h not in S, the number of distinct second units among ORIGINAL complete words of length at least2 that start with h.
additional_original_word_head_bound.b_h: The number of distinct codewords already in B(S) that start with h.
additional_original_word_head_bound.proof: A word starting with h not in S cannot start with singleton h. Its first code therefore has length at least2 and must match the word's first two units. Different second units require different h-headed first codes, regardless of their ultimate lengths or any prefix comparability elsewhere. At least d_h such codes are necessary. Only max(0,d_h-b_h) must be counted beyond the mandatory subcode. Different h classes cannot share the same code.
additional_original_word_head_bound.L_S: L(S)=|B(S)|+sum over h not in S of max(0,d_h-b_h).
additional_original_word_head_bound.singleton_head_caution: For h in S, do NOT forbid longer codes beginning h and do NOT apply the same distinct-second branch requirement. For example C={a,ab} is UD even though a is singleton and ab has the same head. Such longer codes may already occur in B(S).
additional_original_word_head_bound.nontrivial_floor: If every unit of A occurs somewhere in W and S is proper, a missing singleton unit must lie in some actually used longer code. Hence |C|>=|S|+1 as well; use max(L(S),|S|+1).
additional_original_word_head_bound.all_singletons_case: If S=A, every longer string over A already decomposes into singleton codes, so adding it as a code violates UD. This case permits identity only and cannot witness the required nontrivial usage.
additional_original_word_head_bound.unobserved_unit_caution: If A contains unused working units, proper S alone does not prove actual long-code usage: a missing singleton might be unused. The sufficient premise is that an actually occurring unit is outside S. Do not silently infer nontriviality from unused table entries.
additional_original_word_head_bound.head_tail_caution: Only head deficits are added in this proposal. If a later independent tail bound is also considered, head and tail deficits cannot simply be added: one new code can satisfy both. No such extra bound is used here.

finite_necessary_screen.enumeration: Enumerate every exact singleton set S containing S0. For the stated all-observed alphabet, retain proper S only. Test the finite mandatory B(S) for free UD and compute the displayed lower bound for every surviving S.
finite_necessary_screen.global_lower_bound: The minimum of max(L(S),|S|+1) over surviving proper S is a necessary lower bound for any nontrivial compatible full code. An empty surviving set excludes nontriviality. A minimum greater than22 excludes the declared at-most22-entry class.
finite_necessary_screen.positive_ceiling: A minimum at most22 means only NOT EXCLUDED. It gives neither a compatible extension C, coverage of longer words, exact minimal codebook size, a source alphabet assignment nor a human reader.
finite_necessary_screen.no_search_expansion: This proposal does not select any26/28-entry solver, source-word search or adaptive codebook construction.

optional_graph_path_lemma.graph: Use the directed edge a->b for each original whole two-unit word ab in W2. This orientation differs from the suffix-side reversal convention.
optional_graph_path_lemma.claim: Every vertex on a directed path from a forced singleton in S0 to a forced singleton in S0 must itself be singleton in any compatible freely UD code.
optional_graph_path_lemma.proof: Suppose some vertex on that path is outside the exact singleton set S. Choose a subpath v0,v1,...,vm between consecutive visits to S that contains this excursion. Its endpoints are singleton, all internal vertices are not, and m>=2. Every edge vi vi+1 is therefore a mandatory two-unit code. The full concatenation v0...vm has two distinct code parses by alternating adjacent pairs and using the singleton endpoint or endpoints as necessary. If m is even, one parse is [v0],[v1v2],...,[v(m-1)vm], and the other is [v0v1],[v2v3],...,[v(m-2)v(m-1)],[vm]. If m is odd, one parse is [v0v1],[v2v3],...,[v(m-1)vm], and the other is [v0],[v1v2],...,[v(m-2)v(m-1)],[vm]. Their first code lengths differ, so the code sequences are distinct even when some vertex labels repeat. This contradicts UD.
optional_graph_path_lemma.conservative_closure: ForwardReach(S0) intersect BackwardReach(S0) in this fixed graph is therefore a forced-singleton set. Paths may use the same starting/ending singleton. A path with no internal non-singleton offers no collision and merely preserves already forced vertices.
optional_graph_path_lemma.scope: The collision concatenation need not itself be an attested word. That is sufficient for FREE UD and insufficient for a claim against a grammar-restricted non-UD writer. This graph lemma can aid understanding, but enumerating all S and directly testing B(S) avoids relying on it as a computational shortcut.

hand_examples.reason: The table is suffix-free and therefore UD. It contains singleton a and longer ab beginning a. Any rule banning all longer codes with singleton heads would be false.

hand_examples.purpose: UD strictly beyond both instantaneous directions
hand_examples.reason: Not prefix-free because a prefixes ab; not suffix-free because a suffixes bba. The only initial prefix-overlap residual is b; comparison against bba gives residual ba; ba is prefix-incomparable with every code, so the residual closure terminates without collision. This is a small hand UD check, not an executed solver.

hand_examples.forced_collision: [ab,c] and [a,bc] both concatenate to abc. Therefore b must also be singleton in a freely UD completion.

hand_examples.purpose: No parity exception for a longer excursion
hand_examples.assume: b and c are not singleton

hand_examples.purpose: The necessary bound is not a sufficiency result
hand_examples.bound: B is UD and the head bound including the nontrivial floor is1.
hand_examples.remaining_impossibility: Any freely UD code over a unary alphabet has at most one codeword: two different lengths collide by repeating each to a common total length. A one-code table covering both lengths2and3 must have code length dividing both, hence length1. Thus no nontrivial UD completion exists here despite the permissive necessary bound.

human_and_meaning_scope: This is a broad negative-test family, not a complete newly selected human writer. A general UD table may require whole-word lookahead/backtracking and need not have the simple end-first or start-first reading of962/961. Any positive construction still owes the actual source-character table, table-length/lookup costs, punctuation, names, physical continuation and ordinary source-language meaning. Fixed injective letter substitution preserving word boundaries also preserves source word identities/frequencies; old source-conditioned frequency failures remain where those assumptions apply. No source or native word meaning is assigned.

priors_and_duplicates.retained_result: The exact old98-unit inventory is not freely UD; its canonical BPE procedure was not contradicted. That old fixed-table collision and the finite residual algorithm are known, not rediscovered here.
priors_and_duplicates.difference: This proposal derives mandatory short subcodes for every possible singleton set of an unknown small table, instead of evaluating one already supplied98-unit codebook.

General UD includes codes in neither instantaneous class. Their left/right quotient closures are not valid premises here. Only original complete one/two-unit words and original whole-word heads are used.
